cards.claim: Under WSD learning rate schedule, the standard Critical Batch Size formula breaks down: larger batch sizes can require less data consumption than smaller batch sizes once training reaches lower loss targets
cards.conditions: WSD learning rate schedule, stable phase, target loss below threshold, Qwen3 MoE and Dense models, 4M-6M batch size range, constant learning rate
cards.effect: Relationship inversion: E(B_large) < E(B_small) after loss drops below threshold (contradicts E(B_large) > E(B_small) formula)
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from training curves showing intersection and inversion of data consumption across batch sizes
cards.quote: However, under the WSD learning rate schedule, we observe that the training curves for varying batch sizes intersect during practice. Specifically, while the relationship holds at relatively higher target losses, this relationship inverts once the target loss drops below a specific threshold, resulting in [E(B_large) < E(B_small)]

cards.claim: The optimal batch size B_e for minimizing data consumption increases monotonically as training loss decreases
cards.conditions: WSD learning rate schedule, stable phase, InternLM2 122M-1B models, batch sizes 64K-7.5M, 50B-120B tokens training
cards.effect: B_e scales monotonically upward with decreasing loss (increasing training progress)
cards.evidence: Empirical fitting analysis shown in Figure 3
cards.quote: As shown in Figure 3, both metrics scale monotonically with decreasing target loss (increasing data volume). This scaling behavior provides the empirical basis for the dynamic batch size scheduling strategy proposed later.

cards.claim: Dynamic batch size scheduling (ramping up from 2M to 6M in 125B-token intervals) produces consistently lower training loss than fixed 4M batch size baseline
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE model, WSD constant learning rate, 4M baseline batch size, 125B-token switching intervals, AdamW optimizer, weight decay 0.1
cards.effect: Training loss curve for dynamic strategy consistently below fixed-batch baseline throughout training
cards.evidence: Empirical results from full-scale pre-training experiments
cards.quote: Figure 4 presents the smoothed training loss trajectory for the Qwen3 MoE model. As illustrated, the curve for the dynamic batch size scheduling strategy consistently lies below that of the fixed-batch baseline, indicating superior convergence.

cards.claim: Dynamic batch size scheduling improves downstream benchmark performance (MMLU and CMMLU) compared to fixed batch size
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE and Dense models, dynamic batch size 2M→6M in 125B-token intervals vs fixed 4M, constant learning rate, 1000 warmup steps
cards.effect: Consistent performance advantage on MMLU and CMMLU benchmarks
cards.evidence: Benchmark evaluation results shown in Figures 5 and 7
cards.quote: Figure 5 further contrasts performance on the MMLU and CMMLU benchmarks, where the dynamic strategy maintains a consistent advantage. Mirroring these findings, Figures 6 and 7 display the training loss and downstream results for the Qwen3 Dense model, which exhibit identical trends.

cards.claim: Scaling learning rate with batch size increases (square-root scaling) does NOT improve performance with dynamic batch sizing; constant learning rate is superior
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE model, dynamic batch size 2M→6M, comparing constant LR vs sqrt(B) scaling, weight decay 0.1
cards.effect: Square-root learning rate scaling provides no performance improvement and may be counterproductive
cards.evidence: Ablation study comparing learning rate scaling strategies
cards.quote: Empirical results in Figure 9 demonstrate that scaling the learning rate offers no performance improvement. This is because higher learning rates exacerbate gradient noise, effectively neutralizing the noise-suppression benefits of larger batch sizes and rendering the scaling strategy counterproductive.

cards.claim: Sequence length extension as alternative to batch size scaling causes immediate performance drop and distribution shift
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE model, seqlen extended from 4K to 5K (250B tokens) and 6K (375B tokens), comparison with micro-batch expansion achieving same global batch size
cards.effect: Immediate performance drop upon increasing seqlen to 6K, non-trivial adaptation period required, risk of learning preference shift
cards.evidence: Ablation study comparing sequence length extension vs micro-batch scaling
cards.quote: Empirical results in Figure 10 reveal an immediate performance drop upon increasing seqlen to 6K, suggesting a non-trivial adaptation period is necessary to reconcile the distribution shift. Although the model eventually recovers, the risk of a learning preference shift toward long-context sequences makes this approach less desirable for standard large-scale pre-training.

cards.claim: The effectiveness of dynamic batch size scheduling is heavily dependent on weight decay strength
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE model, comparing weight decay 0.1 vs 0.01, dynamic batch size 2M→6M strategy
cards.effect: With weight decay 0.01, initial advantage of dynamic strategy diminishes and nearly vanishes during training
cards.evidence: Ablation study comparing weight decay settings
cards.quote: By reducing the coefficient to 0.01 on the Qwen3 MoE model, we observe in Figure 11 that the initial advantage of the dynamic strategy diminishes and nearly vanishes as training progresses. These findings indicate that the effectiveness of dynamic batch sizing is coupled with regularization strength; specifically, the full benefits of the strategy are contingent upon an optimal weight decay setting.

cards.claim: Dynamic batch size scheduling maintains performance advantages in the decay (annealing) phase of WSD schedule with high-quality data
cards.conditions: Qwen3 MoE model, decay phase with linear learning rate decay to 10%, 100B tokens, dynamic strategy maintains 6M peak batch size
cards.effect: Performance advantage sustained through annealing phase despite distribution shift
cards.evidence: Extended training experiment in decay phase
cards.quote: Figure 12 demonstrates that the performance advantage of the dynamic strategy is sustained throughout this phase. This confirms the robustness of our approach against data distribution shifts, validating its effectiveness in standard large-scale training pipelines.

cards.claim: The minimum batch size threshold B_t (required to reach target loss) increases monotonically as training loss decreases
cards.conditions: WSD learning rate schedule, stable phase, InternLM2 models 122M-1B, variable batch sizes 64K-7.5M
cards.effect: B_t scales upward monotonically with decreasing loss, indicating critical batch size grows during training
cards.evidence: Theoretical derivation and empirical fitting on loss curves (Figure 3)
cards.quote: Physically, B_t and B_e quantify critical batch size thresholds: B_t is the minimum batch size needed to reach a target loss, and B_e is the batch size that yields minimum data consumption. As shown in Figure 3, both metrics scale monotonically with decreasing target loss (increasing data volume).
